sources.snippet: Large language models achieve superior performance on tasks that require extended reasoning, but long chains of thought make the KV cache a severe memory bottleneck. Existing KV cache compression methods share one paradigm: score each cached token by some estimate of how much it will matter later, and keep the top-scoring ones. sources.title: Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for ... - OpenReview
sources.snippet: Random Attention keeps the prompt and evicts uniformly at random within each attention head, computing no score at all; across four models and six reasoning tasks, it matches the strongest baseline in task performance while delivering 32-43% higher throughput than that method when deployed with vLLM.
